claims.text: Official Mercedes documentation: the new E‑Class uses MBUX touchscreen displays and touch‑sensitive "Touch Control Buttons" on the steering wheel (capacitive detection) and a widescreen cockpit — i.e., Mercedes describes the E‑Class controls as primarily touch/capacitive. ([media.mbusa.com](https://media.mbusa.com/news/the-new-e-class-intelligence-that-excites))

Edmunds (first‑drive) reports the new E‑Class "got rid of almost all the physical controls in the cabin," leaving a central touchscreen (MBUX) and a single slim strip of touch‑sensitive buttons under the display. ([edmunds.com](https://www.edmunds.com/car-news/2024-mercedes-benz-e-class-first-drive.html?msockid=23e96163d4b66c9525957724d5206d47))
claims.about: E‑Class removal of physical controls; touchscreen focus

claims.text: TopGear's E‑Class interior review criticizes Mercedes' move away from tactile controls: "the last surviving buttons have been deleted in favour of haptic steering wheel touchpads, which ... are beyond frustrating." ([topgear.com](https://www.topgear.com/car-reviews/mercedes-benz/e-class/interior))
claims.about: Reviewer critique of E‑Class touch‑centric controls

claims.text: Cars.com summary for the Audi A6 e‑tron: the cabin is highly digitized — "no real physical controls outside of a volume knob, start button and short rocking shifter" — with most functions accessed via the infotainment screens. ([cars.com](https://www.cars.com/articles/2026-audi-a6-s6-sportback-e-tron-review-electric-maturity-512401/))
claims.about: Audi A6 e‑tron minimal physical controls; screen‑centric interface

claims.text: Road & Track's A6 e‑tron review: Audi swaps many traditional controls for sweeping digital displays and screens; reviewers found the system logical and generally easy to operate despite the many touch panels. ([roadandtrack.com](https://www.roadandtrack.com/reviews/a65613518/year-make-model-tested-1727778965-1754482231/))
claims.about: Reviewer view that Audi's digital interface is polished and usable
